slides.texte_overlay:
How to get respect while
staying completely calm
Slow down when others speed up. In a heated discussion, talk slower and lower. The calm voice in a loud room naturally becomes the one people follow.
Ask a question instead of attacking. "What do you mean by that?" Calm questions make rude comments fall flat and keep you calmly in control.
Keep your word, especially on small things. Respect isn't won in one big moment. It's built every time you do exactly what you said you'd do, on time.
Disagree without insulting. "I see it differently." Clear but polite disagreement earns more respect than both shouting and silent agreement ever will.
Before: I lost my cool in every argument. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a calmer head that keeps me steady when things heat up.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I lost my cool in every argument. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A calmer head keeps me steady under pressure.

slides.texte_overlay: Protect your time politely. "I can't today, but I can tomorrow at ten." Respecting your own schedule teaches others to respect it too, without any conflict.
Let your actions answer criticism. Don't fight every comment with words. Steady results over time silence doubts far better than any argument.
